design:
GOAL: after compaction, inject one deterministic state block built only from this session's journal rows. No LLM summary, no regex, no truncation, no API key. Pattern = observation masking + external store (F5, F6, F7): the block holds whole facts and exact pointers; full text stays in context.db.

0. CHANGES vs INPUT DESIGN (skeptic fixes)
- Pointer lines and footer were dead ends (F18) -> pointers now call ctx_resume(seq:N), an exact primary-key read.
- Exit code showed MAX not last (F17) -> join on last-failure seq.
- canonical(command) merged quoted text (F20) -> quote-aware state machine.
- 'Compute at PostToolUse if too slow' was a fallback chain and the timing claim was false (F14b) -> ONE path: compute at the compaction re-injection point only.
- events table gets an agent column; eviction cap is per session, not per project (F21).
- LIMIT 64 was arbitrary -> derived from B.
- Decay table is a checked-in integer literal, not Math.pow at run time.
- ADR-0009 'cut at a code-point boundary' removed (F16).

1. BUDGET
B = 2048 UTF-8 bytes (Buffer.byteLength). Reasons: ADR-0009 fixes 2 KB; 5x under the 10,000-char spill cap (F3); Claude Code already restores CLAUDE.md, plan, git status and 5 files (F2), so the block only adds: requests, open errors, changed paths, indexed sources.
Derived constants: MIN_LINE = 24 B (shortest possible pointer line). MAX_CAND_PER_SECTION = floor(B / MIN_LINE) = 85 (no more lines can ever fit, so the bound loses nothing). INLINE_CAP = floor(B * 5 / 16) = 640 B.

2. JOURNAL (context.db, ADR-0002)
events(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, session_id TEXT NOT NULL, worktree TEXT NOT NULL, agent TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, tool TEXT, key TEXT, path TEXT, ok INTEGER, exit_code INTEGER, bytes INTEGER NOT NULL, body TEXT, turn INTEGER NOT NULL)
INDEX ev_sess(session_id, kind, seq); INDEX ev_key(session_id, kind, key, seq).
Rows from hook JSON fields only:
- prompt (UserPromptSubmit): body = prompt, bytes, turn = prompts so far in session.
- edit (PostToolUse/Failure of Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit): path = tool_input.file_path (absolute, cc-hooks.md:1701), key = 'edit\0'+path, ok.
- read: path only, never selected (CC re-reads files itself).
- cmd (Bash / shell / ctx_execute): key = tool+'\0'+canon(command); ok = 1 from PostToolUse, 0 from PostToolUseFailure; exit_code: take error string up to first '\n' (indexOf), if it startsWith('Exit code ') parse the rest with a digit loop (charCode 48..57) into an integer, else NULL. is_interrupt = true -> no row.
- toolerr (any other failed tool, incl. MCP): key = tool+'\0'+stableJSON(tool_input) where stableJSON = recursive serializer with keys sorted bytewise. Resolved by a later ok=1 row with the same key.
- index (ctx_index): key = source label.
canon(command): one pass over code points with state {OUT, SQ, DQ, ESC}. OUT: whitespace (space, tab, CR, LF) sets a pending-space flag, emitted once before the next non-space char; leading/trailing dropped. SQ/DQ/ESC: copy char as-is. No regex. (/tmp/wf4/sk/canon.mjs)

3. CANDIDATES (every query has WHERE session_id = :current; live run shows session_id is unchanged across compaction, F19; empty id -> inject nothing)
- last_request: newest prompt, pinned.
- earlier_requests: next newest prompts, LIMIT 85. Line = whole body if bytes <= 640, else pointer '- #<seq> (<bytes> B) ctx_resume(seq:<seq>)'. Never a cut string.
- open_errors (one query, F17 fix):
  WITH g AS (SELECT key, MAX(CASE WHEN ok=0 THEN seq END) lf, MAX(CASE WHEN ok=1 THEN seq END) ls, SUM(ok=0) nf FROM events WHERE session_id=? AND kind IN ('cmd','toolerr','edit') GROUP BY key HAVING lf IS NOT NULL AND (ls IS NULL OR ls < lf)) SELECT g.*, e.tool, e.exit_code, e.body, e.turn FROM g JOIN events e ON e.seq = g.lf ORDER BY g.lf DESC LIMIT 85.
  cmd line shows the canonical command whole if <= 640 B, else pointer to ctx_resume(seq:lf).
- files_changed: SELECT path, MAX(seq), COUNT(*) WHERE kind='edit' AND ok=1 GROUP BY path ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 85.
- indexed_sources: SELECT key, MAX(seq), COUNT(*) WHERE kind='index' GROUP BY key ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 85.
User decisions = their own prompts. No classifier, no role, no directive.

4. SCORE (integers only)
w: last_request pinned, open_error 900, prompt 500, edit 400, index 200.
a = current_turn - item_turn. DECAY_PPM = checked-in literal int array for H = 4 turns, a = 0..32: round(1e6 * 2^(-a/4)); a > 32 -> 0. decay = 250000 + floor(750000 * DECAY_PPM[a] / 1e6) (floor 0.25, so an old open error stays).
r = count - 1 (failures of the key, edits of the path, index calls of the source). bonus = 1 + (31 - Math.clz32(r + 1)).
score = floor(w * decay / 1e6) * bonus. cost = byteLength(line) + 1 (+ section header bytes when the section is first used).

5. SELECTION (budgeted lazy greedy)
used = bytes(open tag) + bytes(footer) + pinned line cost.
gain_k = score * 70^k / 100^k (integer floor, k = lines already taken in that section) -> sections stay mixed.
ratio = floor(gain_k * 1e6 / cost) (integer).
Sorted array by (ratio desc, seq desc, key asc bytewise). Loop: take first; if its k is stale, recompute ratio and reinsert by binary search; else add if used + cost <= B, else skip (smaller items may still fit). m <= 4 * 85 = 340, so O(m^2) worst case is < 0.2 ms. Never cut an item.

6. RENDER
<context_mode_state session="ID" upto="MAXSEQ">
sections in fixed order: last_request, open_errors, files_changed, earlier_requests, indexed_sources; lines inside by seq asc.
footer: 'more: ctx_search(queries:["<your terms>"], scope:"session")' then </context_mode_state>.
No clock, no user role, bare tool names (PR12), framed as data.

7. POINTER TOOL (no dead end)
ctx_resume gains one optional integer param seq. ctx_resume(seq:N) = SELECT kind, tool, body FROM events WHERE seq=? AND session_id=:current; returns the whole body (an explicit request, so the 2 KB block budget does not apply). Wrong session or no row -> reply names the session and the max seq. Primary-key read, no FTS lag, no partial-match collision (F18).

8. ONE DELIVERY PATH PER AGENT (ADR-0009 table kept)
- Claude Code, Codex, Qwen, ZCode: compute inside SessionStart(source=compact). Nothing precomputed, no PreCompact hook. Live-proven for Claude Code (F19).
- Gemini, Copilot CLI, VS Code: compaction hook runs INSERT OR REPLACE INTO meta(k,v) VALUES('pending_compact:'||sid, upto). Next prompt hook: BEGIN IMMEDIATE; DELETE FROM meta WHERE k=? RETURNING v; COMMIT. A row back -> compute and inject once. Atomic, so two hooks never both inject.
- Pi, OpenCode 2, Kiro: as ADR-0009.
Claude Code also needs the PostToolUseFailure hook registered (else nothing is ever ok=0).

9. LATENCY (F14b, measured)
Algorithm 4.3-8.9 ms in-process. Whole SessionStart(compact) process p95 48.6 ms vs bare Node p95 45.6 ms on this Mac: Node startup alone breaks GS6. Compaction is rare, and precomputing on every PostToolUse would add the cost to the hottest hook, so the single path stays at compaction time. GS6 needs a decision for all hooks (see open questions), not a compaction-only workaround.

10. IDEMPOTENCY
Output = f(rows with session_id = S and seq <= upto). Same rows -> same bytes (10/10 runs identical; foreign rows ignored). No sha/state table needed.

11. STORAGE EVICTION (replaces v1 fixed-priority FIFO, F12)
Cap per session (PRD E7, 5 MB = SUM(bytes)). Checked after insert, inside the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE. When over cap, delete in this order until under cap, oldest first in each class: (1) read rows; (2) index rows except the newest per key; (3) cmd/toolerr rows of resolved keys; (4) edit rows except the newest per path; (5) prompt rows except the newest 85. Open-error rows and their last failure are never deleted. Every class is a single DELETE ... WHERE seq IN (SELECT ... ORDER BY seq LIMIT n).

12. ADR-0009 EDITS
(a) ':40 and :57 cut at a code-point boundary' -> 'whole items only; budget check before each add'. (b) add PostToolUseFailure for Claude Code. (c) add ctx_resume(seq). (d) resolve PRD JSONL-per-session vs ADR-0002 events table (F21).

13. GOLDEN TESTS (GP6, node only, no API key)
G1 10k rows, 10% foreign -> bytes <= 2048, no foreign text.
G2 fail 'npm test' then pass -> not listed; 'npm run build' exit 2 only -> listed 'exit 2'.
G3 'npm  test' resolves 'npm test'; 'echo \"a  b\"' does NOT resolve 'echo \"a b\"'.
G4 800-byte 'ğ'x400 prompt -> pointer ctx_resume(seq:N), no partial char.
G5 3,000-byte last_request -> pinned pointer, block valid.
G6 edits of a.ts at seq 3 and 9 -> one line 'a.ts x2 (#9)'.
G7 two runs -> byte-identical; add foreign row -> identical.
G8 no clock, no 'directive', no 'mcp__' in output.
G9 empty session id -> no output.
G10 is_interrupt failure -> no row.
G11 failures exit 2 then exit 1, no success -> line shows 'exit 1' (F17).
G12 ctx_resume(seq) of another session's seq -> refused, names current session.
G13 algorithm p95 of 20 in-process runs on 10k rows < 15 ms.
LIVE (owner's logged-in Claude Code, no key, about $0.07 per run reported): the F19 harness, stream-json input [prompt, '/compact', question], plugin via --plugin-dir, asserts hook_response 'SessionStart:compact' outcome success and that the model echoes a marker from the block.

risks: Node startup alone measures p95 45.6 ms on this Mac, so GS6 (p95 <= 40 ms for every hook) fails before any work; the compaction hook measured p95 48.6 ms. This is a project-wide issue, not one the compaction algorithm can fix.
Half-life 4 turns, weights 900/500/400/200, gamma 0.70 and floor 0.25 are chosen, not measured; tune them on the owner's real journals.
Exact canonical key: 'npm test' and 'npm test -- --watch' are different keys, so a fix run with other flags leaves the old error open. Accepted over guessing.

A command that exits non-zero as normal (grep with no match exits 1) becomes an open error until the same command succeeds. v1 handled this with a stdout heuristic (src/exit-classify.ts); v2 has no rule yet.

The live harness's stream-json '/compact' trick worked on Claude Code 2.1.283; a later CLI version could change slash-command handling in headless mode.
ctx_resume(seq) is a new tool parameter; it adds to the tool schema size that TECH-SPEC tracks.
open_questions: GS6: Node startup alone breaks p95 40 ms on this Mac. Raise the budget, measure CPU time not wall time, or use a long-lived process? This decides every hook, not only compaction.
Should a non-zero exit with output (grep no-match) count as a failure? It needs a rule that is not a text heuristic.
PRD-v2 says journal = JSONL per session; ADR-0002 says events table in context.db. Which one wins?
Should PostCompact compact_summary (3,019 chars in the live run) be stored as a searchable source? It is LLM text, so it is not part of the block, only of ctx_search.
Kiro, ZCode and OpenCode 2 delivery paths still need live checks per ADR-0009.

design:
GOAL
One keyless command the owner runs by hand on his Mac before dev work. It uses his Claude Code Max login (Keychain) and, if ready, his ChatGPT-logged-in Codex. It never runs in CI. One path per step, no fallback chains, no regex, no text cutting.

ENTRY POINTS (both call the same script; not two paths)
1. Terminal: `node e2e/live/run.mjs [--agents claude,codex] [--models haiku|sonnet|opus|all] [--cases routing,deny,compact,hooks] [--concurrency 3]` (= `npm run e2e:live`).
2. In Claude Code: repo file `.claude/commands/e2e-live.md`. Body: run `node e2e/live/run.mjs $ARGUMENTS` with run_in_background, wait, then show `e2e/live/out/<ts>/report.md` as is. Running from inside a session is safe because the child env is built from scratch (F14, run7).

PREFLIGHT (no model calls)
- realClaude(): one structural rule, never executes an unknown file. For each dir in PATH (split on ':'), c = dir+'/claude'; if it exists, r = fs.realpathSync(c); read the first 4 bytes of r. Accept iff bytes are a Mach-O magic (cf fa ed fe / ce fa ed fe) or ELF (7f 45 4c 46), or the nearest package.json above r has name '@anthropic-ai/claude-code'. A '#!' script without that package.json (claude-worktree, vibetree shims) is skipped. First accepted wins. None → FAIL preflight and print every candidate with its realpath, so the owner sees why (F13).
- Then `bin auth status` with the scratch env → JSON.parse; require loggedIn && authMethod==='claude.ai', else SKIPPED claude: not logged in.
- codex: `codex login status` with CODEX_HOME=<tmpCodexHome> (see below); compare the first line to the fixed string 'Logged in using ChatGPT' (string equality). Else SKIPPED with that line.
- Other agents: PATH lookup + fs.accessSync(X_OK), no shell. Missing → SKIPPED not installed. Present, no driver → SKIPPED no driver yet.
- `npm run build` once. Plugin dir = build output with .claude-plugin/plugin.json and .mcp.json. Missing bundle → FAIL.

CHILD ENV (built from scratch, never inherited)
env = pick(process.env, ['PATH','HOME','USER','LOGNAME','SHELL','TMPDIR','LANG','LC_ALL','TERM']) + {
 ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS:'false'  (F17),
 CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY:'1'  (F20, no writes in ~/.claude/projects),
 CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS:'1'   (F21),
 MCP_TIMEOUT:'30000', CM_E2E_RUN: runId, <V2_DATA_DIR_VAR>: <tmp>/data }.
No CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (Keychain, F4). No ANTHROPIC_*, no CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (F3). Verified shape: run7.

CLAUDE COMMAND (single path)
cwd = /tmp/cm-e2e/<runId>/<case>/proj (fixture, git init; outside /Users/mksglu so no parent CLAUDE.md applies).
`<bin> -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-hook-events --plugin-dir <build> --setting-sources project --no-session-persistence --model <m> --max-budget-usd <cap> --permission-mode default --allowed-tools <case.allow>`
NOT --strict-mcp-config (it drops the plugin server, F17 run4). Turns are written to stdin as JSONL user messages; '/compact' is a turn (F6).
Init gate (hard fail of the case): apiKeySource==='none'; plugin_errors.length===0; mcp_server_errors.length===0; the set of mcp_servers names equals exactly {'plugin:context-mode:<server>'} and its status==='connected'; plugins contains name 'context-mode'. No retry, no second config.

CODEX COMMAND (single path, F12 makes --ignore-user-config unsafe)
tmpCodexHome = /tmp/cm-e2e/<runId>/codex-home containing: auth.json → symlink to ~/.codex/auth.json; config.toml written by the harness ([features] hooks=true, [mcp_servers.context-mode] command/args → build); hooks.json = v2 hooks only.
`CODEX_HOME=<tmpCodexHome> codex exec --json --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust "<turn>"`. The owner's ~/.codex/hooks.json and config.toml are never read because the User layer folder is tmpCodexHome (state.rs:219-243). No dry run, no fallback.

FIXTURES (generated, not committed)
gen(seed) writes files with per-run nonces: nonce = crypto.randomBytes(6).toString('hex') (12 hex chars). routing-large: a 40,000-line log with 3 planted stack traces whose ids are nonces; a 3 MB JSON with 3 target records keyed by nonces. The expected answer = that nonce set. High entropy makes guessing impossible and checking exact.

CASES e2e/live/cases.json — default 12 sessions per model
{id, kind, turns:[...], allow:[...], expect:{...}}
- routing-small x3 ('version field in package.json'): expect firstTool ∈ {Read, Bash, Grep}. ctx tool here = over-routing.
- routing-large x3: expect firstTool ∈ CTX, answer ⊇ nonce set.
- deny x3: (a) Bash curl <url>, (b) Read on a 5 MB file, (c) WebFetch.
- compact x1: turn 1 large task (lands in FTS) → turn 2 '/compact' → turn 3 asks for a nonce only the indexed output has.
- hook-probe x1: one turn that fires SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse.

PARSER (pure data walk)
for line of stdout.split('\n') (skip ''): ev = JSON.parse(line); key = ev.type + '/' + (ev.subtype ?? '').
- 'system/init': keep the FIRST init only (a second init comes after compact, run2/run4); run init gate; CTX = new Set(init.tools.filter(n => n.startsWith('mcp__plugin_context-mode_'))) (prefix compare, not regex; F18).
- 'assistant/': each content block type 'tool_use' → calls.push({id,name,input,turnIdx}).
- 'user/': each tool_result → byId[id].result = {is_error, bytes: Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(content))} (a count, no cut).
- 'system/hook_started'|'system/hook_response': hooks.push({hook_id, event: hook_event, name: hook_name, outcome, exit_code}). No timing here (F19).
- 'system/compact_boundary': compact = compact_metadata.
- 'rate_limit_event/': rl = rate_limit_info.
- 'result/': last = ev (keep only the last; cost is cumulative, F16). turnResults.push({num_turns, permission_denials, result, is_error}).
Derived: firstTool = first call with name !== 'ToolSearch'. cost = last.total_cost_usd. bytesToModel = Σ result.bytes.
Answer check: tokens = result text split on whitespace; each token mapped char by char keeping only 0-9a-f (charCode ranges); pass iff every expected nonce ∈ Set(tokens).

DENY CHECK (not a dead end), DB is the one source
v2 PreToolUse hook, on deny, writes row deny(tool_use_id, tool, alt_tool, alt_input_json) (tool_use_id is in hook input, doc-hooks.md:774; seen in run4 hook log). alt_tool is the FULL callable name (F18).
For each d in last.permission_denials: row = DB deny where tool_use_id = d.tool_use_id (missing row → FAIL 'deny without alternative'). next = first call after d in calls with name !== 'ToolSearch'. recovered iff next.name === row.alt_tool and every key of row.alt_input exists in next.input. Score recovered/denied; gate 3/3 per model.

COMPACT CHECK
compact present; report pre→post (not gated). DB has PreCompact and PostCompact rows for this session (F7). hooks has {name:'SessionStart:compact', outcome:'success'} (F6, run4). Turn 3: first non-ToolSearch call ∈ CTX and answer ⊇ nonce.

HOOK-PROBE CHECK
4/4 events with outcome 'success' in the stream. Timing: each v2 hook writes hook_timing(event, ms) where ms = Date.now() - performance.timeOrigin at exit (includes Node startup). Report p50/p95 from the DB; do not gate live timing (the 40 ms gate lives in local benchmark tests).

VERDICTS
Gates per model: over-routing 0/3, under-routing 0/3, large correctness 3/3, deny recovery 3/3, compact pass, hook-probe 4/4. A failed case re-runs once: PASS (1st pass), FLAKY (fail then pass), FAIL (fail twice). Exit 0 if no FAIL; SKIPPED never fails.

BUDGET AND PLAN GUARD
--max-budget-usd 0.25 haiku, 0.60 sonnet, 1.00 opus (estimate only). After each session read rl: if rl.status !== 'allowed' or unifiedWindows.five_hour.utilization > 0.8, schedule no new sessions, mark the rest SKIPPED: plan window X%. Concurrency 3.

REPORT e2e/live/out/<ISO-ts>/ (gitignored)
- report.md: header (claude version from init.claude_code_version, codex version, plugin git sha, models, five_hour/seven_day before/after). Table | agent | model | case | firstTool | expected | denied→recovered | bytesToModel | compact pre→post | answer | verdict | cost(list, cumulative last) | s |. SKIPPED list. Totals.
- raw/<agent>-<model>-<case>.jsonl, db/<case>.json (normalized rows), env.json = versions and the names (not values) of env keys passed.
- No redaction step: the bundle is built only from allowlisted fields, so there is nothing to redact (no regex). The same field set (versions, init fields, hook outcomes, hook_timing, DB counts, deny rows) is the schema for 'ctx doctor --debug' and the issue template (prototype: /tmp/wf4/full.mjs, a ctx-report block with a sha256 digest).

ESTIMATE (F16 corrected)
Haiku default 12 sessions: routing ~$0.015-0.03 each (ToolSearch adds a turn), deny ~$0.023, compact session ~$0.03 → ~$0.3-0.45 list per run from the Max window; ~10-20 s per session, compact ~30 s → ~1-1.5 min at concurrency 3. '--models all' ~36 sessions, ~$2-3 list, ~5 min. Codex 12 sessions on the ChatGPT plan, cost not measured.

SPEC CHANGES
TECH-SPEC §6.9 (:351-370) and PRD-v2.md:291: delete the CI job, GitHub-environment keys and RC-tag trigger. Replace with 'local by hand, keyless, e2e/live/run.mjs'. Auth column → 'claude.ai login (Keychain)', 'ChatGPT login (temp CODEX_HOME + symlinked auth.json)'. Remove '--strict-mcp-config' from the Claude row and add ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false. Remove '--ignore-user-config' for Codex. Size 220 → 12 per model. Add the deny(tool_use_id, alt_tool, alt_input) and hook_timing tables to the v2 schema. Add one documented data-dir env var.

The owner may delete them. The harness avoids both (F13 structural binary check, F20 CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1).

design:
## Changes from the input design (skeptic pass)
1. CUT the CLI fallback `server.bundle.mjs --doctor`. It is a fallback chain (F19) and it breaks G12-G14. NEW single path: degraded start (B.0).
2. CUT all path text from the report. Paths become typed facts: location enum, has_space, non_ascii, length (F12).
3. Digest is now the full sha256 (64 hex). The 16-char cut was a truncation.
4. Error storage is now per-day buckets with a prune in the same transaction (F20, F21). DB errors are no longer "counted" in the DB. Doctor probes them live.
5. The form no longer depends on '/ctx-doctor' alone (F15). It says: "run /ctx-doctor, or tell the agent: call the ctx_doctor tool" (F18). A dropdown gives fixed reasons when doctor cannot run. The `report` field uses `render: text`, and the block carries no fence of its own.
6. os.release is parsed as digits plus a '+suffix' flag (F22). The `busy_7d` row is cut (no source for it). The `v2` label is cut (labels must exist, F9, and v1 is frozen anyway).
7. NEW `deny_7d` row: it shows whether hard denies were dead ends, which is the owner's main concern.

## A. Why v1 debug fails
- bash-only syntax (F3)
- regex redaction leaks (F4)
- 1110 lines of raw text with env values and paths (F5)
- probes that stay green on broken states (F6)
- the form demands PRs and a script that v1 tarballs may not even ship (F1, F5)

## B. v2 report
### B.0 One path: ctx_doctor always answers
- The server bundle never imports `node:sqlite` statically. On start, it runs `await import('node:sqlite')` inside try/catch (F14) and checks the Node minimum.
- If a precondition fails, the server still completes `initialize` and lists ONE tool, `ctx_doctor`. That tool returns the report with `node: ... node:sqlite=fail` and check D2=FAIL plus a one-line fix.
- Only one failure leaves no report: when Node cannot parse the bundle or does not exist. The form covers that with a required `node --version` input and a dropdown reason.
- No CLI, no second script, no fallback.

### B.1 Rows (fixed order, `key: value`, one per line)
The report starts with `ctx-report: 1` and ends with `digest: <64 hex>`.

| key | value grammar | source |
|---|---|---|
| version | semver | bundle constant |
| commit | hex40 | bundle constant (release build) |
| latest_release | semver same\|behind\|ahead, or unknown | `git ls-remote` of the release ref, 3000 ms timeout; no git or no network gives unknown |
| agent | enum(table names)\|other + semver\|unknown | MCP clientInfo.name/.version (F16) |
| install | enum marketplace\|git\|in-process | adapters/table.ts |
| os | enum platform + release digits (+suffix) + enum arch | process, char-scan parser (F22) |
| node | semver; node:sqlite=ok\|fail; sqlite=semver; fts5=ok\|fail | process, pragma_compile_options |
| mcp | client=enum protocol=date server=date | initialize request |
| enforcement | rewrite\|cap\|hint | ADR-0008 row |
| config | mcp=match\|missing\|differs hooks=k/4 timeouts=default\|user-kept extra_keys=int duplicates=int | structural diff: host config parsed into an object vs the generated object (counts only) |
| v1_leftovers | int; data_dir=enum(none\|home-dot-dir\|other) size_mb=int | detectV1(agent) (ADR-0011:58) |
| v1_leftover (0..8 rows) | file-kind enum + JSON pointer + reason enum | each pointer segment is a key in our generated schema or a decimal index, otherwise `<user-key>` |
| v1_leftovers_more | int | count of findings beyond row 8 |
| project | source=enum worktree=main\|linked agents_seen=enum list | adapter source + DB |
| paths | data_root=enum(default\|env-override) has_space=bool non_ascii=bool max_len=int | the facts behind #548 and #712, with no path text |
| db | integrity=ok\|fail fts5=ok\|fail schema=int size_mb=int busy_probe_ms=int | real context.db: PRAGMA quick_check, FTS5 'integrity-check', and one timed BEGIN IMMEDIATE/ROLLBACK (live probe, replaces the stored busy count) |
| index | sources chunks empty_sources events_7d (ints) | COUNT(*) on the real tables (#1014) |
| hook (4 rows) | Event ok\|FAIL median_ms=int max_ms=int | D5: spawn the real hook entry 5 times with the shipped fixture, check the output shape; `FAIL` when median > 40 |
| hook_error (0..5 rows) | CODE Hook count=int first=date last=date | B.3, ORDER BY count DESC, code |
| hook_error_more | int | number of (code, hook) pairs not shown |
| deny_7d | total followed alt_failed abandoned (ints) | B.3b |
| checks | D1..D10 = OK\|WARN\|FAIL\|UNKNOWN | ADR-0010 |
| digest | sha256 hex of every line above it, joined by \n | computed |

Size: worst case 2652 B / 38 lines (F13). The limit is 4096 B, held by construction: row counts are fixed and every value has a bounded grammar. Lists are chosen by score (top 5 by count, first 8 in detect order). The rest is COUNTED, and no string is ever cut. A unit test renders the max-width fixture and asserts < 4096.

### B.2 Cells: typed scanners, no regex, no free text
```
cell(kind, v): v==null -> 'unknown'
 int|ms|mb : Number.isSafeInteger(v) && v>=0 ? String(v) : '<invalid>'
 semver    : drop one leading 'v'; split('.'); 2..4 parts, each 1..6 chars, all '0'-'9'
 relver    : scan chars: digits and '.' -> keep; at the first other char stop and add ' +suffix'
 hex40     : length 40, chars in 0-9a-f        (bundle constant only)
 date      : split('-') -> lengths [4,2,2], all digits
 enum      : SET.has(v) ? v : 'other'
 bool      : v===true ? 'yes' : v===false ? 'no' : '<invalid>'
 jsonptr   : segments from GENERATED_KEYS (a Set) or all-digit; else '<user-key>'
 any failed check -> '<invalid>' (the whole value is dropped, never part of it)
```
- No path, env value, config value, file body, error message or command line reaches the output.
- Path facts are computed (has_space = p.includes(' '), non_ascii = any charCode > 127, max_len) and printed as bool/int only.
- Error codes come from a closed enum in src/errors.ts. An unknown code is stored as E_OTHER.

### B.3 Error storage (bounded by codes x 4 hooks x 8 days)
```
CREATE TABLE hook_error_day(code TEXT NOT NULL, hook TEXT NOT NULL, day INT NOT NULL,
  count INT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(code,hook,day)) WITHOUT ROWID;
-- on a hook error, inside the hook's BEGIN IMMEDIATE (measured 0.1-0.26 ms, F21):
INSERT INTO hook_error_day VALUES(?,?,?,1) ON CONFLICT(code,hook,day) DO UPDATE SET count=count+1;
DELETE FROM hook_error_day WHERE day < :today-7;
-- report:
SELECT code,hook,SUM(count) c,MIN(day),MAX(day) FROM hook_error_day GROUP BY code,hook ORDER BY c DESC, code LIMIT 5;
```
- Only errors that are not about the DB get written (E_HOOK_SHAPE, E_HOOK_SLOW, E_PROJECT_SOURCE_MISSING, E_CONFIG_DRIFT, E_V1_CONFLICT, E_DENY_ALT_FAILED, E_OTHER).
- E_DB_BUSY and E_DB_CORRUPT cannot be stored in a broken DB, so doctor measures them live in the `db` row.
- The error path only runs on errors, so a healthy hook adds 0 ms.

### B.3b Deny follow-through (proves no dead ends)
```
CREATE TABLE deny_day(day INT, alt TEXT, denied INT, followed INT, alt_failed INT,
  PRIMARY KEY(day,alt)) WITHOUT ROWID;
```
- PreToolUse deny: denied+1. It also stores pending=(session, alt tool) in the existing session row.
- The next PreToolUse in that session:
  - its tool == alt -> followed+1
  - PostToolUse of alt with an error -> alt_failed+1
- abandoned = denied - followed (a SELECT, nothing stored).
- Same transaction as the deny, same prune rule.

### B.4 Digest
- Full sha256 of the body. It flags hand edits and broken pastes. It is not a security feature.
- Owner triage (local, Claude Code or node): `gh issue view N --json body`. Then, line by line:
  - skip lines that start with ```
  - `i = line.indexOf(': ')`; key = slice(0, i), value = slice(i+2)
  - recompute the digest and parse the typed cells back.

design:
GOAL: deny only when MEASURED or COMPUTED output exceeds a budget, decided from a parse tree, never from text patterns, and every deny carries one exact working call.

1. PARSER (one module, no dependency, no regex, about 12 KB; prototype /tmp/wf4/proto/sh.mjs)
- Lexer: a character state machine. An operator table is matched longest-first (&&, ||, |&, <<-, <<<, >>, &>, >&, <&, >|, <>, <<, ;, |, &, (, ), <, >, newline). Quote states: ', ", \\. $( ) and backticks are scanned with balanced counting. Heredoc delimiters are queued, and on the next newline each body is consumed line by line until a line equals the delimiter (with <<- leading tabs dropped). The body becomes DATA on the redirect, never tokens.
- Parser: recursive descent.
  list := pipeline (sep pipeline)*
  pipeline := [!] command (| or |& command)*
  command := simple | ( list ) | { list } | if | while/until | for, each followed by redirs
  simple := assigns* words* redirs*. A digit-only word just before a redirect is the fd.
- $( ) and backticks (also inside double quotes) are parsed recursively, depth <= 8. Their stdout is consumed by the outer word, so it never reaches the tool output.
- Unsupported (case, function definitions, [[ ]], process substitution, arithmetic for) raises ParseError.
- AST node: {type:'simple', assigns[], argv:[{text, kinds:['lit'|'sq'|'dq'|'var'|'sub']}], redirs:[{op, fd, target, heredocBody}], subs:[AST]}.
- Complexity: O(n * |OPS|) lexing with |OPS| = 21; O(tokens) parsing; O(n * depth) worst case with substitutions. Measured 3.9 ms cold and 0.31 ms warm for 2 KB.

2. TYPED TABLES (data, not patterns)
- WRAP: {timeout:1 operand, time, nice, nohup, stdbuf, command, builtin, noglob, env (skips K=V), sudo}. This is the same list Claude Code strips (permissions.md:237). The table gives the number of operands to skip after the wrapper's flags.
- PRODUCER[argv0 basename] = {class, priorBytes, fileOutFlags, stdoutAliases, subcommandArity}.
  Classes: net (curl 32K, wget, defaultFile), file (cat/less: size computed with stat of the literal path args), walk (find, ls -R, tree), search (grep, rg), build (npm, pnpm, gradle/gradlew, mvn, sbt, cargo, go test), vcs (git log/diff/show, by subcommand), tiny (echo, pwd, wc, which, --version), none (cd, mkdir, mv, export).
- SINK[argv0] = function(parsed argv) -> bound in bytes, or null:
  head/tail: -c N gives N; -n N gives N * meanLineLen(signature), with a default of 10 lines.
  wc, grep -c/-q/-l: 64 B or 4 KB.
  Any stage with > file, >> file, or &> file (target not /dev/stdout) gives 0.
  tee, sort, uniq, awk, jq, xargs: null, meaning they pass bytes through.
- Flags are parsed per spec: the short cluster '-sL', '--opt=value', and '-o value'. This is argv walking, not text search.

3. SIZE PREDICTION (algorithmic, measured)
- Signature = argv0 basename after unwrap + subcommand (for vcs/build/gh/docker/kubectl) + sorted flag-name set + arg-kind string (L literal, V var/sub, P path, U url) + (walk class only) the first path literal.
- context.db table sig_stats(sig PK, n, ewma_log, hist BLOB = 32 log2 buckets, mean_line_len).
- PostToolUse records bytes = len(stdout) + len(stderr) for a Bash response (shape {stdout, stderr, interrupted, isImage}).
- Credit assignment: if the command has exactly one output-reaching pipeline, record under that pipeline's producer signature, adjusted for its sink. Always record the whole-command signature too.
- Update cost O(1). p90 query: scan 32 buckets.
- predicted(sig) = (k*prior(class) + n*p90(sig)) / (k + n) with k = 3 (shrinkage toward the class prior). For the file class, use the exact stat size instead.
- Pipeline bytes = min(producer bytes, every sink bound along the pipe).
- List bytes = sum over items; if = max over clauses; loop = body * item count (8 if the items are not literal).
- Command substitutions add 0. Background (&) jobs add their pipeline's bytes.

4. DECISION (one path per tool; no fallback chains)
- Bash / run_shell_command:
  a. ParseError, or length > 64 KB: ALLOW + record {reason:'unparseable', code}. This is the one documented path.
  b. bytes = estimate(AST).
  c. bytes <= BUDGET (16384, one constant): ALLOW.
  d. Otherwise, if ctxAvailable(session, agent_id) and NOT repeatDeny(session, commandHash): DENY with the translated call (step 5).
  e. Otherwise ALLOW + record the reason.
  repeatDeny: the identical command was already denied once in this session. So a second identical attempt is never blocked. This guarantees no dead end even if the ctx server breaks mid-session.
- Read: no limit given and stat size > BUDGET: DENY. The alternatives are Read {file_path, offset:1, limit: floor(BUDGET / meanLineLen(file))} (still a real Read, which keeps read-before-edit working) or ctx_execute. Read with offset/limit: ALLOW. Cost: one stat, under 0.1 ms.
- Grep: output_mode files_with_matches or count: ALLOW. For content mode, signature = (path, glob/type, mode, head_limit); predict from history and the head_limit bound. If over budget: DENY with the same Grep plus output_mode:'count' (Claude Code's count total is exact, tools-reference.md:338), or with head_limit = floor(BUDGET / meanLineLen).
  A probe (rg --count from the hook) is rejected: a process spawn plus the walk cost is far above 10 ms on large trees.
- Glob: ALLOW. Claude Code caps it at 100 paths.
- WebFetch: ALLOW by default. Claude Code returns an extraction model's answer, not the raw page (tools-reference.md:602), and the v1 unconditional deny broke artifacts (#938, #984, #1006). Record per-host bytes; DENY only if host p90 > BUDGET.
  A HEAD request is rejected: one RTT (50-300 ms) breaks the hook budget, and Content-Length says nothing about the extracted answer.
- ctxAvailable: a row in context.db sessions(session_id, agent_id, server_pid, last_seen), written by the MCP server on initialize (keyed by CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID), or by PostToolUse when any ctx_* call is seen for that session_id/agent_id. Never machine-global (fixes #1055, #1037, #794).

5. DENY MESSAGE = deterministic translation from the AST and tool input
- Bash: 'context-mode: predicted ~{bytes} B ({source: history n=… | prior class=… | stat}), budget 16384. Same command, full run, only your printed result returns:\\nctx_execute {"language":"shell","code":<original command verbatim, JSON-escaped>,"intent":<tool_input.description if present>}'.
  The code is the original string. It is not rebuilt, so quoting is never changed. JSON.stringify does the escaping.
- Read: Read {file_path, offset, limit} plus ctx_execute {language:'shell', code:"cat <single-quoted path>", intent}. Quoting algorithm: wrap in single quotes; each ' becomes '\\'' (a character loop).
- Grep: Grep {…same, output_mode:'count'}.
- WebFetch: ctx_index {url} then ctx_search {queries:[prompt]}.
- Retry routing: the model's retry is a ctx_* MCP call. PreToolUse never modifies ctx_* input (PRD §6), and ctx_execute runs the command in the sandbox, indexes the full output and returns only what was printed. That is not truncation by us. An identical Bash retry passes (repeatDeny).

6. DEBUG RECORD (feeds issue reports)
Each PreToolUse decision writes one journal row: {ts, agent, agentVersion, session, agent_id, tool, sig, astShape (node types only, no args), parse:{ok, errCode, ms}, predicted, source, n, budget, ctxAvailable evidence (row id, age), decision, hookMs}.
A debug script prints the last N rows with commands hashed. The issue template asks for that block, so v2 bug reports carry the exact decision path.

risks: The hook wall budget (p95 <= 40 ms) is not reachable: empty Node alone measured p95 37-65 ms here, and parse plus SQLite adds about 8-10 ms. The budget must be restated as added cost over bare Node, or the hook must use Node's compile cache and a single bundled file. This needs a decision.

The hand-written parser covers a subset (no case, function definitions, [[ ]], process substitution). Anything outside it goes to allow + record. That is safe but loses savings, so the unparseable rate must be read from the journal and the subset extended if needed.

The size model is only as good as its history. On cold start, class priors decide; a wrong prior gives false denies (cost: one extra turn, as F7 shows) or misses. Credit assignment in compound commands is approximate.
repeatDeny allows an identical retry, so a stubborn model can bypass the deny. It is accepted, because otherwise a broken ctx server is a dead end.
Read deny with Haiku 4.5 / Opus 4.6 must keep offset/limit Reads allowed, or Edit fails (read-before-edit).
A ctx availability row written by the MCP server uses the spawn session id; after /clear the hook session id changes (env-vars.md:383). Until a ctx_* call is seen in the new id, denies are off.

design:
GOAL: deny only when the computed output size of a call is over one budget. The decision comes from a parse tree plus measured statistics, never from text patterns. Every deny names one exact call that works. Nothing is cut by us.

0. WHERE THE DECISION RUNS (one transport per agent, one decision core; not a fallback chain)
- One module decide.mjs (parser + tables + estimator), loaded once in the long-lived MCP server. The server keeps context.db open and sig_stats in a Map.
- Claude Code: PreToolUse hook {type:'mcp_tool', server:'context-mode', tool:'ctx_route', input:{tool:'${tool_name}', input:'${tool_input}', session:'${session_id}', agent:'${agent_id}', agentType:'${agent_type}'}, timeout:5}. No Node start-up. The decision takes 1.26 ms in the server (F13). The hook process does no DB work, so PRD P4 holds. If the server is not connected, Claude Code runs the tool. That is the defined 'ctx unavailable means allow' behavior, for this session only. No isMCPReady, no session-id table.
- Pi, OpenCode 2: in-process extension; it imports decide.mjs directly.
- Codex, Gemini, Qwen, Copilot CLI, VS Code, Kiro, ZCode: command hook = one bundled file, node --compile-cache, opens context.db readOnly and runs one indexed SELECT per signature. Cost: about 16 ms CPU on top of Node's 33 ms (F4). The budget text must change to 'added CPU over bare node <= 20 ms' for command-hook agents (open question 1).
- ctx_route handler rule: it is async and never waits behind a running ctx_execute (executor stays off the event loop). Test: route p99 < 5 ms while ctx_execute runs a 30 s job.

1. PARSER (no dependency, no regex, about 12 KB)
- Lexer: a character state machine. Operators are matched longest-first against a fixed array (21 entries). Quote states: ', ", backslash. $( ) and backticks use balanced counting. Heredoc bodies are read line by line until a line equals the delimiter; the body is data on the redirect.
- Grammar: list := pipeline (sep pipeline)*; pipeline := [!] cmd ((| | |&) cmd)*; cmd := simple | ( list ) | { list } | if | while | until | for, then redirs.
- Strict rejection (fix F14c): the tokens '[[', '((', 'case', 'function', a word followed by '()', '<(' and '>(' raise ParseError(code). They are never accepted as plain words. Golden cases cover each code.
- Substitutions are parsed recursively up to depth 8. Their stdout goes into the outer word, so they add 0 bytes.
- Input over 10,000 chars: ParseError('too_long'), the same limit Claude Code uses (perm.md:290).

2. TYPED TABLES (data, not patterns)
- WRAP[name] = {operands, stopIf}: timeout{1}, time, nice, nohup, stdbuf, builtin, noglob, env{skip K=V}, sudo, command{stopIf:['-v','-V']}, xargs{onlyIfNoFlags:true}. This fixes F14b and matches perm.md:237-241.
- PRODUCER[basename] = {class, prior, fileOutFlags, stdoutAliases, subcmd}. Classes: net, file, walk, search, build, vcs, tiny, none. Unknown argv0 uses class 'unknown' with a prior of 4096.
- SINK[basename](argv) -> bytes or null. head/tail -c N gives N; -n N gives N * meanLineLen(producerSig), 10 lines by default; wc and grep -c/-l/-q give 64 B. tee, sort, uniq, awk, jq and xargs give null (they pass bytes through).
- Redirects are fd-aware (fix F14a): stage stdout goes to a file only when the redirect fd is null or 1 and the op is one of >, >>, >|, &>. Stage stderr is handled the same way with fd 2, or with &>. bytes(stage) = stdoutBytes * [stdout reaches the tool] + stderrBytes * [stderr reaches the tool]. Each producer has a measured stderrShare (default 0.1).
- Flags are read by walking argv: '-sL' clusters, '--k=v', '-o v'.

3. SIZE ESTIMATE (measured, O(1) per signature)
- sig = basename(argv0 after unwrap) + subcmd + sorted flag names + arg-kind string (L/V/P/U) + (walk class only) the first path literal.
- sig_stats(sig PK, n, hist BLOB of 32 log2 buckets, sumLines, sumBytes). meanLineLen = sumBytes / sumLines.
- pred(sig) = (k*prior + n*p90) / (k + n), k = 3. File class: exact stat size of each literal path (no prior). Missing file: 0.
- Cold-start fix for #817 (F14e): when n = 0 and class = net, the decision is 'allow + record' and not deny, unless the same host has a p90 over the budget. So the first small curl passes, and the history learns. Every other class keeps its prior.
- Pipeline = min(producer, each sink bound). List = sum. if = max over branches. for = body * literal item count; when the items are not literal, 8 (a stated prior that gets recorded). while/until with '< file' = body * (stat(file) / meanLineLen) (fix F14d). Without input it uses 8.
- PostToolUse (async: Claude Code uses a command hook with async:true, so it is off the critical path) records len(stdout) + len(stderr) and the line count. The whole-command sig is always recorded. The producer sig is recorded only when the command has exactly one pipeline that reaches the output, and its sinks are all null.

4. DECISION (one function per tool)
decideBash(cmd, ctx):
  ast = parse(cmd); on ParseError -> ALLOW, journal {parse:'err', code}
  b = estimate(ast)
  if b <= BUDGET (16384) -> ALLOW
  if seen(session, agent, sha1(cmd)) -> ALLOW, journal 'repeat'      // no dead end: an identical retry runs
  mark(session, agent, sha1(cmd)); DENY(message from step 5)
- Read (no offset/limit) with stat > BUDGET: DENY once per (session, agent, path). An identical retry of the same Read passes, so read-before-edit (F10) always has a path. The alternative is ctx_execute with intent (full content indexed, ranked return). It never offers 'limit N' (no truncation, F15). Read with offset/limit: ALLOW.
- Grep content mode: pred from sig (path, glob/type, mode); over budget: DENY with the same Grep and output_mode:'count' (the exact total, tools.md:338), or ctx_execute rg with intent. No head_limit suggestion.
- Glob: ALLOW (capped at 100). WebFetch: ALLOW. Record bytes per host; DENY only when the host p90 > BUDGET. The alternative is ctx_fetch_and_index then ctx_search. claude.ai artifact hosts are never denied (#938/#984/#1006): they are a named entry in the host table, not a pattern.
- Subagents: agentType is read from the input. The server reads the agent definition (.claude/agents/<type>.md frontmatter 'tools:' list, parsed as YAML keys). If it has a tools list without a ctx_* entry, ALLOW + journal. Built-in agent types: open question 4.

5. DENY MESSAGE (built from the input, the original string kept as-is)
'context-mode: predicted ~{b} B ({src}: n={n}, p90={p90} | prior {class} | stat), budget 16384. Run the same command here; the full output is indexed and only the part that matches your intent returns. Tool: {exactToolName}\n{JSON.stringify({language:"shell", code: cmd, intent: tool_input.description ?? "<state what you need>"})}\nIf you must run it with Bash anyway, send the identical command again.'
- exactToolName is the name the host shows (mcp__context-mode__ctx_execute, or the plugin-scoped name), fixed per adapter at build time. It lets ToolSearch 'select:' load the deferred tool in one step (F13).
- The code is the original string. JSON.stringify escapes it. Nothing is rebuilt.

6. DEBUG JOURNAL (feeds the v2 issue form)
One row per decision: {ts, agent, agentVersion, transport:'mcp_tool'|'inproc'|'command', session8, agentType, tool, sig, astShape (node types only), parse{ok, code, ms}, pred, src, n, p90, budget, decision, repeat, decideMs}. 'context-mode debug --last 20' prints the rows with argv hashed. The issue form asks for that block.

7. GOLDEN CASES (current 17 plus these; all must pass)
'find / -name x | grep -v foo 2>/dev/null' deny; 'command -v curl' allow; 'f(){ ls; }; f' ParseError(func) allow; '[[ -f x ]] && cat x' ParseError(dbracket) allow; 'while read l; do echo $l; done < big.txt' (big.txt 1 MB) deny; cold 'curl -s https://ifconfig.me' allow + record; 'curl -sL URL' with host p90 40 KB deny; Read of a 300 KB file deny, then the identical Read allow; Grep content with pred 50 KB -> deny with output_mode count.

8. E2E WITHOUT API KEYS (owner's Claude Code login)
scripts/e2e.sh runs: env -u ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL -u ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS claude -p "<case prompt>" --model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 --setting-sources project --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config e2e/mcp.json --output-format stream-json --verbose. A node checker reads the stream-json and asserts, per case: a tool_result is_error that contains 'context-mode: predicted'; one of the next 2 tool_use events is ctx_execute (ToolSearch may come first); its code contains the original command; the final result is correct. About $0.026 per case (F7, F13).
risks: The mcp_tool transport is Claude Code only. The other 7 command-hook agents still pay about 33 ms CPU for Node plus about 16 ms for the decision, so they cannot meet a 20 ms CPU or 40 ms wall budget. Someone must decide on the budget wording.

I did not measure the full mcp_tool hook round-trip inside Claude Code; only the 1.26 ms in-server decision is measured. If the server's event loop is blocked by a sync job, every Bash call waits up to the hook timeout.
Claude Code puts 'PreToolUse:Bash hook error:' in front of the reason. Compliance was seen on Haiku only (2 deny runs). Opus and Sonnet are not tested.
ctx_execute is a deferred tool in Claude Code, so each first deny costs one extra ToolSearch turn (F13).
The repeat rule lets a stubborn model run the identical command on its second try. This is the price of having no dead end.
Read deny once per path costs one turn on files the model wants to edit (Haiku 4.5 and Opus 4.6 need a full read first).
Class priors are guesses until history fills: false denies cost 1 turn, and misses flood once. The cold-start allow for curl gives up savings on the first large curl for each host.
Credit assignment in compound commands is approximate. Only commands with a single pipeline update producer signatures.
The PowerShell tool (#1212) needs its own parser. Kiro deny delivery is unverified.
ADR-0008 (head/tail cap, rewrite wrapper) must be replaced by this design, or the no-truncation rule is broken.
open_questions: Budget: does 'p95 <= 40 ms wall' (TECH-SPEC:39) or '<= 20 ms CPU, no DB' (PRD:23) apply to command-hook agents, given bare Node uses 33 ms CPU? Proposal: added CPU over bare node <= 20 ms, with a read-only SQLite SELECT allowed.
Should ADR-0008 be marked superseded by this algorithmic deny?

In Claude Code, do the mcp_tool hook substitutions keep commands with newlines and heredocs exactly (only a single-line command with single quotes was tested)? Passing '${tool_input}' as a whole JSON string, then JSON.parse in the server, avoids most of the risk.
Built-in subagent types (Explore, Plan, general-purpose): do they get MCP tools? A custom agent's tools list can be parsed from its file, but built-ins have no file.
Does an explicit Read with offset/limit that returns the whole requested range count for read-before-edit on Haiku 4.5? The docs do not say.
Is BUDGET = 16384 right, given that Claude Code already spills Bash output above about 30,000 chars to a file with a 2,000-char preview?
